title: God’s Name Is Great in Israel

reflections.title: "The Wrath of Man Shall Praise You"

reflect.text: When people oppose God and His people, their anger can feel scary. Yet God is always in control. Scripture tells us that even human fury will end up praising Him. Throughout history, enemies have raged, but God used their actions to reveal His own power. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "the wrath of man shall be made to redound to the glory of God." The greatest example was the cross, where the anger of wicked men ended up fulfilling God's wonderful plan to rescue us.

God also sets a clear boundary on how far any enemy can go. He permits trouble only up to a point, saying "thus far and no farther." Like a miller who holds back the river and only lets through enough water to turn his wheel, God restrains the rest of man's rage. You do not need to panic when the world turns against truth. God will not let you be tested beyond your strength, and He will turn every trial into a reason to praise Him.

questions: When you face anger or unfair treatment from others, how does knowing God is in control give you peace?
In what ways have you seen God bring good out of a difficult or hostile situation?
reflections.prayer: Lord, help us to remember that no anger in this world is greater than Your power. When we face opposition or trial, keep us from fear and teach us to trust Your loving boundaries. May our lives bring You praise in every season. Amen.

reflections.title: God's Deliverance and Our Response

reflect.text: Because God has delivered us, the psalm calls us to bring our gifts and fulfill our vows to Him. Many people view giving as an unwanted chore or a fee to attend church. But true worship begins when we realize that everything we own comes from God's hand. Giving our offerings back to Him is not personal charity, but a humble act of thanksgiving. Honoring God with what we have protects our hearts from loving temporary earthly things and turns our gaze toward eternal riches.

questions: How does knowing that Jesus broke the power of sin and condemnation bring you comfort today?
How can offering your resources back to God change how you view your money and possessions?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You for sending Jesus to break the weapons of sin and set us free from all condemnation. Help us to see everything we own as a gift from Your hand. Give us joyful hearts that love to give back to You in gratitude for all You have done. Amen.

unsupported.text: In Psalm 76, God shows Himself as the mighty protector who shatters the weapons of war. On the cross, Jesus won this decisive victory for us. When He cried out that His work was finished, He broke the power of sin, guilt, and the enemy. Charles Spurgeon described Jesus smashing every arrow of sin across His knee. Because Jesus took the punishment for our wrongs, no accusation can condemn those who trust in Him. Our spiritual enemies have been completely disarmed.
unsupported.problem: According to D1, Spurgeon describes Jesus dashing the arrows of sin to pieces on the anvil of the cross using His woes as a hammer; it is the sword of Satanic power that He snaps across His knee, not the arrows.
